notes: SKEPTIC verdict: all 4 entries CONFIRMED, class_after = AUDITED (0 EQUIVALENT, 0 REFUTED, 0 test owed). All four mutants match the draft exactly (re-derived via buildmut + mutant_view: capability_version idx0=compare F->T, idx1=hash F->T; capability_changes idx0=compare F->T, idx1=hash F->T). Each toggles only the generated CatalogEntry.__eq__ or __hash__. Independently reproduced: unmutated kill file 51 OK, and each mutant 51 OK (survives, not killed). Each is genuinely observable (not EQUIVALENT), shown by direct execution: compare mutants flip ==, the version hash mutant flips hash-equality, the changes hash mutant makes the file_artifact entry raise TypeError. No semantic reader depends on the eq/hash participation: exhaustive grep across aisef2/ validation/ tests/ finds nothing that compares two CatalogEntry objects with ==/assertEqual, hashes one, or uses one as a set member or dict key; every consumer reads attribute VALUES or keys dicts by subject_kind/probe_id (entry as value), and dataclasses.replace builds entries via __init__. Checked the two plausible non-registered guards and cleared both: (1) test_v21_identity reads values and digests the probe modules' own bytes, not catalog.py, and does not touch entry eq/hash; (2) the committed conformance ruling (closure-evidence/v2/v2.1/CONFORMANCE-RULING.json) has 12 rows and does NOT include aisef2/probe/catalog.py, so its sha256 drift guard R.check() does not pin catalog.py bytes -- there is no file-digest guard that would kill these mutants (and the campaign reporting them as survivors in a 2.1 file confirms no byte guard is run as a kill file for these targets). Ran test_cycle2_wp201 on baseline and the two strongest mutants: identical outcome (delta zero; its failures are missing-closure-evidence env errors, and its entry-exercising Catalog tests pass on both). One immaterial author slip noted: the diagnostics dataclasses.replace is at bundle/diagnostics line 226, not 224. Agree with the author's acceptance-scope recommendation to the owner: record as a known limit (esp. the capability_changes hash mutant's latent unhashable-file_artifact edge and the unpinned compare=False prose), do not add tests merely to pin the flags.
